bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42497421 (fribidi): Heap-use-after-free WRITE 8 found by fuzz target fribidi-fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42497421
bug_description.normalized: The witness drives FriBidi to explicit embedding level 124 before an overflowing FSI, so the FSI raises isolate_level without raising embedding level. `compact_neutrals()` then merges the FSI's following `ON` run across isolate levels and redirects the FSI run's `next_isolate` away from the final tail run while that tail run still keeps `prev_isolate == fsi`. N1/N2 rewrites the merged FSI run and the newline run to `LTR`, and the second `compact_list(main_run_list)` call at line 1261 later merges `newline` with the final `LTR` tail run without checking isolate level, so `merge_with_prev()` writes through the freed `fsi` pointer still stored in the tail run's `prev_isolate`.

source.description: First project statement that consumes the fuzzer-supplied UTF-32 witness and materializes the vulnerability-relevant bidi-type stream used to build FriBidi runs.
source.value_from: The staged 268-byte `poc` is interpreted as 67 UTF-32LE `FriBidiChar` values: `U+202D`, 33x `U+202A`, `U+202D`, 27x `U+202A`, `0x20202020`, `U+2068`, `U+2020`, `U+000A`, and `0xFFFFFF20`. The exact tail types are `LTR`, `FSI`, `ON`, `BS`, and `LTR` respectively.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.var: list->prev, list, RL_TYPE(list->prev), RL_TYPE(list), RL_LEVEL(list->prev), RL_LEVEL(list), RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL(list->prev), RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL(list), RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list->prev), RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list)
root_cause.description: At the later `compact_list(main_run_list)` call at line 1261, `newline` and `post_ltr` have both been rewritten to adjacent `LTR` level-0 runs, but the predicate still does not require equal isolate levels. The fix adds `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL(list->prev) == RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL(list)` here so that second cross-isolate merge never reaches the crashing `merge_with_prev(post_ltr)`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. During `merge_with_prev(post_ltr)`, `post_ltr->prev_isolate` still aliases the freed `fsi` run, so line 93 performs the heap-use-after-free write through that dangling isolate-link pointer.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `WRITE of size 8` at `merge_with_prev /work/build/../../src/fribidi/lib/fribidi-bidi.c:93:40`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled witness first becomes FriBidi's internal bidi-type stream here; every later explicit-level decision, bracket-state materialization, isolate-link edge, type rewrite, and compaction predicate on the crashing path derives from these classified entries.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The staged `poc` contributes the exact 67 UTF-32LE codepoints described in `source.value_from`.

fine_trace.note: Source. The exact witness classifies into 62 explicit controls (`LRO`, 33x `LRE`, `LRO`, 27x `LRE`) followed by `LTR` for `0x20202020`, `FSI` for `U+2068`, `ON` for `U+2020`, `BS` for `U+000A`, and `LTR` for `0xFFFFFF20`. `gen.tab/gen-bidi-type-tab.c` initializes the bidi table to `LTR`, and `gen.tab/packtab.c` emits `FRIBIDI_GET_BIDI_TYPE(x)` to return that default when `x >= 0x110000`, which is why the out-of-range tail word becomes the final `LTR` run.

The witness tail's bracket state is materialized here. `pre_ltr`, `fsi`, `newline`, and `post_ltr` are not `ON`, so line 91 stores `FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET` for them directly. `dagger` is `ON`, but `gen.tab/gen-brackets-type-tab.c` defaults the bracket-type table to 0 and `gen.tab/unidata/BidiBrackets.txt` has no `2020` entry, so `fribidi_get_bracket(U+2020)` also yields `FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET`.

fine_trace.var: char_type, bracket_type, run, last, run->type, run->bracket_type
fine_trace.note: FriBidi materializes those entries as heap `FriBidiRun` nodes. After the explicit-control prefix, the witness tail is five single-character runs in list order: `pre_ltr(0x20202020)`, `fsi(U+2068)`, `dagger(U+2020)`, `newline(U+000A)`, and `post_ltr(0xFFFFFF20)`; `new_run()` at `lib/fribidi-run.c:44` allocates each node, `FRIBIDI_IS_ISOLATE(char_type)` keeps `fsi` in its own run, and line 147 copies step 2's all-`FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET` tail bracket state into the run fields.

The 62 leading `LRO/LRE` runs are all accepted explicit pushes. Starting from base level 0, these lines raise the current embedding state by 2 per run until the tail segment is reached with `level == 124`: `pre_ltr` is processed at that even level and the later `fsi` still sees the same 124 state. This is the 125-level boundary condition called out by the fix commit.

When the `fsi` run is processed, `for_run_list (fsi_pp, pp)` begins at `pp->next`, so the scan skips the FSI itself, sees `dagger` (`ON`) and `newline` (`BS`) as non-letters, then reaches `post_ltr`, whose `LTR` type from step 1 makes line 752 set `fsi_base_level = 0`. These lines therefore compute `new_level = 126`, store the FSI run itself as `RL_LEVEL=124, RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL=0`, increment `isolate_level` to 1 for following runs, and then refuse to push because 126 exceeds max 125; the following `dagger` run therefore inherits level 124 in isolate level 1.

The `newline` run is `FRIBIDI_TYPE_BS`, so explicit-level processing breaks here before writing the current level 124 into it. `newline` therefore keeps its initialized `level` 0 while retaining `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL=1` from the loop header, and the following `post_ltr` run is never processed at all, so it stays at default `level` 0 / isolate level 0 from step 3. Those two level-0 tail runs become the later crashing pair.

The isolate-link builder connects runs by isolate level, not by list adjacency. For the witness tail it creates iso0 chain `pre_ltr -> fsi -> post_ltr` and iso1 chain `dagger -> newline`; in particular `post_ltr->prev_isolate = fsi` and `fsi->next_isolate = post_ltr` at this point.

fine_trace.var: list->prev, list, RL_LEVEL(list->prev), RL_LEVEL(list), RL_TYPE(list->prev), RL_TYPE(list), RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list->prev), RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list)
fine_trace.note: At the first `compact_neutrals(main_run_list)` call at line 1037, `fsi` and `dagger` are adjacent, both neutral, both level 124, and their `run->bracket_type` fields from step 3 are `FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET`, so this predicate merges them even though their isolate levels are 0 and 1. This is the earlier cross-isolate compaction the patch's second hunk forbids.

Merging `dagger` into `fsi` frees the `dagger` run and rewires only `dagger`'s isolate links: line 85 sets `newline->prev_isolate = NULL`, and line 94 sets `fsi->next_isolate = newline`. `post_ltr->prev_isolate` is not touched because `post_ltr` was the old iso0 successor of `fsi`, not `dagger->next_isolate`, so the stale-alias precursor is now `post_ltr->prev_isolate == fsi` while `fsi->next_isolate` no longer points back to `post_ltr`.

depends_on.via: RL_LEVEL (list->prev) == RL_LEVEL (list) && ((RL_TYPE (list->prev) == RL_TYPE (list) || (FRIBIDI_IS_NEUTRAL (RL_TYPE (list->prev)) && FRIBIDI_IS_NEUTRAL (RL_TYPE (list))))) && RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list) == FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET && RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list->prev) == FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET

fine_trace.note: N0 finds no bracket pair in this witness, then lines 1213-1216 overwrite every surviving run's `bracket_type` with `FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET` and re-run `compact_neutrals()`. For this witness no new same-level neutral pair exists, so the list shape stays `pre_ltr -> merged fsi+dagger -> newline -> post_ltr`, but the later line-1261 `RL_BRACKET_TYPE(...) == FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET` checks now depend on this re-cleared state in the reviewed tree.

In N1/N2, the merged `fsi+dagger` run is still neutral. `get_adjacent_run()` sees `pre_ltr` behind it at the same level, and its forward isolate link now points to `newline`; because `newline->isolate_level > fsi->isolate_level`, lines 165-169 skip that cross-isolate run to the sentinel, so both sides resolve to `LTR`. Line 1255 rewrites the merged run to `LTR`, making the first line-1261 pair `pre_ltr` + merged `fsi+dagger` both `LTR` at level 124.

The `newline` run is also neutral. After step 9 it has no same-isolate neighbors (`prev_isolate` and `next_isolate` are null), so this same assignment resolves both sides to the level-0 embedding direction `LTR` and rewrites `newline` from `BS` to `LTR`. The final tail pair is now `newline(LTR, level 0, isolate 1)` followed by `post_ltr(LTR, level 0, isolate 0)`.

fine_trace.var: list->prev, list, RL_TYPE(list->prev), RL_TYPE(list), RL_LEVEL(list->prev), RL_LEVEL(list), RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list->prev), RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list)
fine_trace.note: In the second `compact_list(main_run_list)` call at line 1261, `pre_ltr` and the merged `fsi+dagger` run now match on type `LTR`, level 124, and step 10's `FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET` state, so `compact_list()` enters `merge_with_prev()` on that pair. This is the freeing merge recorded in the ASan free stack at `compact_list -> fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels_ex:1261`.

When that first line-1261 merge frees the `fsi` run, the repairs at lines 85/90/92 still do not clear `post_ltr->prev_isolate`. `second->next_isolate` is `newline`, so line 85 rewrites only `newline->prev_isolate = pre_ltr`; the line-90 fallback is bypassed; and line 92 writes through `second->prev_isolate` (`pre_ltr`). `post_ltr` is therefore the surviving run that still holds `prev_isolate == freed fsi` after line 96.

depends_on.via: RL_TYPE (list->prev) == RL_TYPE (list) && RL_LEVEL (list->prev) == RL_LEVEL (list) && RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list) == FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET && RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list->prev) == FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET

fine_trace.var: list->prev, list, RL_TYPE(list->prev), RL_TYPE(list), RL_LEVEL(list->prev), RL_LEVEL(list), RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL(list->prev), RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL(list), RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list->prev), RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list)
fine_trace.note: Later in the same line-1261 `compact_list()` pass, current node `post_ltr` and its previous list neighbor `newline` are adjacent, both `LTR`, both level 0, and step 10 left both `bracket_type` fields at `FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET`. Their isolate levels are still 1 (`newline`) and 0 (`post_ltr`), but this predicate does not compare `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL`, so it takes the second cross-isolate merge and reaches the crashing `merge_with_prev(post_ltr)`.

Sink. In `merge_with_prev(post_ltr)`, `second->prev_isolate` is still the freed `fsi` run from step 14, so line 93 writes `next_isolate` through that dangling pointer. This matches the saved ASan `heap-use-after-free WRITE of size 8` at `merge_with_prev:93`.

depends_on.via: RL_TYPE (list->prev) == RL_TYPE (list) && RL_LEVEL (list->prev) == RL_LEVEL (list) && RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list) == FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET && RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list->prev) == FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET

free_context.description: The `fsi` run is freed by the first `merge_with_prev()` inside the same `compact_list(main_run_list)` call at line 1261, before the second merge writes through `post_ltr->prev_isolate`.

format.name: UTF-32LE FriBidiChar sequence
format.contract: Exactly the staged 268-byte `poc`, interpreted by `fribidi-fuzzer` as 67 little-endian 32-bit `FriBidiChar` values: `U+202D`, 33x `U+202A`, `U+202D`, 27x `U+202A`, `0x20202020`, `U+2068`, `U+2020`, `U+000A`, and `0xFFFFFF20`. This contract is limited to that witness, which reaches explicit level 124 before the FSI, overflows the FSI to isolate level 1 without raising the embedding level, and leaves the exact level-0 `newline`/`post_ltr` pair consumed by the crashing `compact_list()` pass; it does not generalize to other embedding-control strings or isolate layouts.
